title: Magnetar Systems  Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive ML inference across private VPC. Key themes: reserved GPU sizing (A100 vs H100), isolation/VPC/KMS requirements, burst strategy for spiky workloads, expected scaling timeline, and security/SOC2 evidence. Next steps: pricing + capacity proposal, security pack, pilot benchmark run.
next_steps: Redwood to send draft pricing + capacity recommendation (Lena)
SE to schedule benchmark run and share perf template (Diego)
Send security docs and SOC2 report link (Jules)
Customer to confirm 30-day pilot window and stake holders (Priya)
action_items: Owner: Lena Park; Item: Draft pricing and capacity recommendation for 4-week pilot; due_date: 2026-03-09
Owner: Diego Morales; Item: Schedule perf benchmark and share match-to-prod workload template; due_date: 2026-03-11
Owner: Jules Reed; Item: Share SOC2/ISO docs + KMS integration notes; due_date: 2026-03-06
Owner: Priya Shah; Item: Confirm pilot participants and time window; due_date: 2026-03-08
transcript:
00:00 Lena (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:06 Priya (CTO): Priya Shah here, hi.
00:08 Tom (Infra Lead): Tom, hi.
00:10 Sara (Head of ML): Sara Brooks, morning.
00:12 Ethan (Security): Ethan Cole from security.
00:15 Lena: Great, from Redwood we have Diego SE and Jules on security docs. We'll run through your current stack then sizing and burst strategy.
01:02 Lena: Can you give us a bit of context on the workload and why dedicated vs hosted?
01:10 Priya: Sure. We're running a mix of real-time scoring for risk models and some batch enrichment. The real-time is low latency, 50-150ms target for single requests, and we have spiky traffic — e.g., payday spike, marketing blasts. We evaluated hosted but want isolation and predictable throughput.
01:35 Diego (SE): Got it. For predictable throughput you'd be looking at Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with optional burst into shared or burst capacity. Can you give numbers: tokens per request, requests per second peak?
01:48 Sara: Typical prompt ~350 tokens, but we use longer context for history occasionally up to 2k tokens. Peak concurrent requests can hit ~80 rps during spikes, sustained baseline more like 8-12 rps.
02:06 Tom: We also have strict data residency and want VPC peering. No traffic egress to public internet for inference.
02:14 Lena: Understood. On VPC we support private deployments and Dedicated in a VPC — we can lock networking down with peering and private link. Jules, do you want to mention KMS?
02:27 Jules (SE): Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. We also provide audit logs and can point to our SOC2 report.
02:34 Ethan (Security): For SOC2 and encryption at rest we need the report and details on key rotation and log retention.
02:40 Jules: We'll share the SOC2 and our ISO notes, and a short runbook on KMS flows.
03:05 Diego: Back to sizing — given 2k token windows and latency target, H100s would be the recommendation for headroom; A100 might work for lower-cost profiles but could push latency slightly. Do you have model family in mind?
03:18 Sara: We're testing open models: a trimmed Llama-family variant and a private finetuned LLM. Both are ~13-70B depending on variant.
03:29 Diego: For 13B quantized we can get more throughput per GPU but for heavier 70B variants you'll want H100s with more memory. Also we can host multiple model variants and route by policy.
03:46 Tom: How does burst work? We sometimes have 200 rps for 30-60 minutes. We can't permanently commit to huge reserved capacity.
03:55 Lena: We offer a reserved baseline and configured burst policy — you commit to a set of GPUs (monthly) and we can allow autoscaling/burst on top with a price multiplier. There's also a managed Warm Pool option to reduce cold-starts.
04:12 Diego: Another lever is batching and KV cache for prefix reuse — if many requests share prefix info we can reduce GPU compute. The caching works with private models too, but keys live in your VPC.
04:26 Sara: Are there limits to burst duration?
04:29 Lena: No hard limit but sustained burst beyond agreed tiers will be billed or require adjustment to the committed pool. For a pilot we typically set a soft burst cap.
04:40 Priya: We'd like a predictable cap so we can budget. Can you illustrate cost delta A100 vs H100?
04:48 Lena: We'll send a draft pricing sheet. Quick rule of thumb: H100s about 2x A100 for cost but often better latency for same model size and fewer nodes for high-memory models.
05:05 Diego: On scaling expectations — how quickly can Dedicated scale up?
05:09 Lena: Provisioning a new dedicated pool in-region is typically a few hours to a day depending on inventory; for higher SLAs we do reserved procurement. For pilot we can provision smaller clusters same day in manyRegions.
05:22 Tom: Network topology — do you support private link or VPC peering only?
05:28 Jules: Both options. For strict air-gapped on-prem we offer Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane. For cloud VPC peering we use private link and dedicated ENIs.
05:42 Ethan: Audit logs retention policy? Legal may ask for 1 year of logs.
05:46 Jules: We can ship logs to your S3/GCS and retain as required; default retention is 90 days but adjustable with enterprise add-on.
06:05 Sara: For model rollout we need canaries and version pinning — can you support gradual rollouts?
06:12 Diego: Yes — per-route model pinning, canaries, automatic fallback to a compatible variant if a new model regresses. We also have tracing hooks to pull latency and token-level cost.
06:26 Priya: For compliance, SSO/SAML and RBAC are must-haves.
06:30 Jules: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls.
06:40 Tom: Storage — where does the model weight reside? On your infra or in our VPC?
06:46 Diego: Models run on Redwood-managed infra for Dedicated but data and request logs can be kept in your VPC if you choose private deployment. For on-prem Private, weights run in customer environment.
07:02 Priya: Can we bring custom finetuned models? We definitely will.
07:06 Diego: Yes; bring-your-own-model is supported, we handle onboarding and perf optimization. We include quantization recommendations and kernel tuning.
07:15 Sara: Any constraints on containerization or custom kernels?
07:19 Diego: We support standard model packages (HF, ggml-ish tarballs) and custom ops are evaluated — sometimes we need a small engineering effort.
07:30 Tom: SLA — what uptime and latency SLO do you commit to on Dedicated?
07:34 Lena: Our Dedicated contracts have SLA tiers; typical is 99.9% uptime and latency targets depend on the model and instance type. We can align on SLOs in the contract.
07:48 Ethan: Will there be pen testing or support for our audit team?
07:52 Jules: We can provide attack surface docs and coordinate a security questionnaire. For enterprise deals we can schedule a pen test coordination.
08:10 Priya: For the pilot we expect to validate p95 latency at production-like load and verify isolation.
08:16 Diego: We'll run a benchmark using your workload template. Ideally we get a day of traffic replay for the spike window.
08:26 Lena: Timing — what's your decision timeline?
08:29 Priya: We're aiming to select a vendor and run pilot in April, with procurement signoff by May.
08:35 Lena: Good — that lines up. We'll follow up with the pricing + recommended pool.
08:45 Tom: A couple of nitty gritty Qs: autoscaling cooldown, data retention for logs, and whether we can pin GPUs to customer tenant.
08:56 Diego: Cooldown is configurable, from 30s to minutes; logs retention we can push to your cloud storage; GPUs are logically isolated per customer in Dedicated pools, and physical isolation is possible depending on procurement.
09:14 Sara: On-billing model: per-token + reserved GPU flat fee?
09:19 Lena: Yes — reserved capacity has a flat commit fee and per-token/per-inference unit for overflow. During pilot we'll show estimated token consumption and cost bands.
09:30 Priya: Any compatibility issues with our latency-sensitive stack? We have an in-house gateway that expects <150ms tail.
09:36 Diego: We'll run profiling; sometimes we recommend edge ingress points or local routing to reduce network hops.
10:02 Lena: Anything else on security or compliance?
10:05 Ethan: Need the SOC2 ASAP and a summary of log formats.
10:10 Jules: We'll attach the SOC2 PDF link and a short log schema.
10:20 Lena: Quick recap and action items?
10:24 Priya: Pilot in April, validate p95 latency and isolation, review pricing and security pack, confirm pilot participants.
10:33 Lena: Great. We'll send the plan and slot for a benchmark run. Thanks everyone.
10:40 Priya: Thanks.
10:42 Tom: Thanks all.
10:44 Sara: Bye.
10:47 Ethan: Bye.
notes: Customer prefers H100 for headroom on 70B models but will consider A100 for 13B quantized variants to reduce cost
Pilot timeline: April pilot, procurement in May
Security wants SOC2 + KMS flow details before pilot start
